A feature tree rebuilt from the skeleton

Source: R/hierarchy.R
vp_feature_tree.Rd

A feature tree rebuilt from the skeleton: each feature gets as parent one of the features it requires directly. When there are several candidates, the least required one is chosen, and the others become cross-tree arrows.

Usage

vp_feature_tree(model)

Arguments

model

A model, from vp_generate() or vp_read(), in its complete or its minimal form.

Value

A tibble with the columns feature, parent (NA for a feature that needs nothing), candidates (how many features it requires directly) and cross_tree (the candidates that were not chosen, separated by commas).

See also

Other hierarchy: vp_atomic_sets(), vp_chains(), vp_common_dependants(), vp_common_requirements(), vp_depth(), vp_downset(), vp_false_optional(), vp_foundations(), vp_implied_requires(), vp_largest_free_set(), vp_largest_unrelated_set(), vp_leaves(), vp_levels(), vp_longest_chain(), vp_longest_decision_chain(), vp_redundant_candidates(), vp_skeleton(), vp_tree_agreement(), vp_upset(), vp_width()

Examples

band <- vp_generate(vp_example("miband3.uvl"), or_graph = TRUE)
vp_feature_tree(band)
#> # A tibble: 8 × 4
#>   feature            parent          candidates cross_tree
#>   <chr>              <chr>                <int> <chr>     
#> 1 Screen             NA                       0 ""        
#> 2 TouchScreen        BLEv42                   1 ""        
#> 3 ContactlessPayment TouchScreen              1 ""        
#> 4 MovementFilter     BLEv40                   1 ""        
#> 5 HeartRateSensor    NA                       0 ""        
#> 6 BLEv40             Screen                   1 ""        
#> 7 BLEv42             HeartRateSensor          2 "Screen"  
#> 8 BT40               NA                       0 ""
